item.title: At least 2 killed, 17 hurt in Brooklyn building collapse
item.description: A major technical rescue operation was ongoing, involving hundreds of firefighters.

item.title: Democrat Scott Colom wins Mississippi Senate race in upset
item.description: Democrat Scott Colom defeated GOP Sen. Cindy Hyde-Smith in the Mississippi Senate race, delivering Democrats an eighth flipped Senate seat after the dramatic race had been up in the air for days.

item.title: Pope declares Peru his "homeland" in final leg of South America trip
item.description: Pope Leo declared Peru his "homeland" as he arrived in Lima at the start of his historic visit​, returning to the place that taught him how to be a pastor.

item.title: Did Jensen Huang Just Destroy America's AI Advantage?
item.description: Billionaires, governments, spies, and the most coveted technology in the world. Author and journalist Patrick McGee explains what we know so far about the scandal surrounding NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang. If you'd like to share your own great question, email us at greatquestion@cbsnews.com.

item.title: 3 killed when SUV crashes into North Hollywood food stand
item.description: At least three people were killed and two others were severely injured when an SUV crashed into a food stand near a Metro bus stop in North Hollywood.

item.title: Nvidia's board preparing to oust CEO Jensen Huang, sources say
item.description: Nvidia's board of directors is preparing to oust CEO Jensen Huang soon, according to two sources, amid allegations Huang had an affair with a woman U.S. intelligence agencies believe was a Chinese asset.

item.title: 2 killed in New York building collapse, Mamdani says
item.description: New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani and FDNY Commissioner Lillian Bonsignore gave an update Wednesday night on a deadly building collapse in Brooklyn as rescuers continued to search for survivors underneath the rubble.

item.title: Inside Nvidia's ties to Megaspeed, company led by alleged Chinese spy
item.description: The investigation into Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's relationship with an alleged Chinese spy has renewed questions about Megaspeed, the company the suspected spy was helping lead. Megaspeed bought nearly $5 billion in AI chips and advanced hardware from Nvidia. Megaspeed denies wrongdoing. CBS News' Isabel Vincent has more.

item.title: Hegseth's group reprimanded for noise at Tomb of Unknown Soldier
item.description: A guard at the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier reprimanded a group of people that included Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth for making noise at the site.

item.title: Bessent relocates from home to military base after Iran threats
item.description: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent has relocated from his home in the Washington, D.C., area to a U.S. military base.

item.title: 7-year-old comes home from school to big surprise: a rescue dog named Wendy
item.description: A 7-year-old Tennessee girl came home from school to find that her parents had surprised her with a rescue dog named Wendy. Tony Dokoupil has the story.

item.title: First snow of the season is coming to Northeast
item.description: Parts of the Northeast could see their first snowfall of the season later this week, as a cold snap spreads over the eastern half of the U.S.

item.title: EU cybersecurity chief fears household goods could be hacked after attacks on commercial fridges
item.description: EU cybersecurity chief Juhan Lepassaar is warning of attacks on home appliances after commercial freezers were recently targeted by hackers across Europe. Juan Andres Guerrero-Saade, a distinguished fellow at cybersecurity company SentinelOne, joins "The Daily Report" to discuss.

item.title: Black students speak about racist incident caught on video: "It was like a slap in the face"
item.description: Two University of Mississippi students were caught on a Ring camera outside the apartment of several Black students making monkey gestures and sounds. Jericka Duncan spoke with the students in the apartment.

item.title: White House warns Democrats of "blatant criminality" over possible probes into Trump administration
item.description: The White House is warning Democratic lawmakers that aggressive oversight of the administration may cross the line into criminality as the new Democratic-led Congress prepares to take office in January. CBS News' Kathryn Watson reports.

item.title: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent moves into military housing due to Iranian threats
item.description: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent has moved out of his home in Washington, D.C., and onto a military base out of concern for his safety, including Iranian threats to his life, officials said. Nancy Cordes has more.

item.title: Dangerous storms break out in Midwest while winter weather hits East
item.description: An outbreak of dangerous storms hit the Midwest on Wednesday, including possible tornadoes, ahead of what will be the first blast of winter weather in the East. The storm system could dump up to 10 inches of snow in some places, bringing sub-freezing temperatures to millions. Rob Marciano has the forecast.

item.title: Unruly passenger and cabin flooding reported on 2 separate flights that landed in Chicago
item.description: A passenger became disruptive on a United Airlines flight from Tokyo to Chicago on Wednesday, officials said, while a flooding incident also forced a separate flight to make an emergency landing in Chicago. Kris Van Cleave has more details.

item.title: Hegseth's group asked by soldier to maintain respect at Arlington National Cemetery
item.description: President Trump traveled to Arlington National Cemetery on Wednesday, laying a wreath in honor of fallen U.S. soldiers. But the cameras also captured a U.S. Army sentinel reprimanding a group that included Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, demanding that they show respect. Charlie D'Agata has more.

item.title: Firefighters dig through rubble of collapsed Brooklyn building
item.description: Several people were killed and more than a dozen were injured Wednesday when a building collapsed in New York City. Fire officials said many others had been pulled from the rubble in a major rescue operation. Lilia Luciano reports from the scene.

item.title: Building adaptive homes for disabled veterans
item.description: Since 2004, the organization Homes For Our Troops has designed and built over 400 houses nationwide for severely injured post-9/11 veterans. Retired Army Sgt. Steven Curry, who lives in one of the homes, joins "The Takeout" to discuss.

item.title: El-Sayed says Van Hollen represents "generational change" as Democrats weigh leadership
item.description: With Democrats still working to elect party leadership for the next session of Congress, Sen.-elect Abdul El-Sayed has thrown his support behind Sen. Chris Van Hollen over current leader Sen. Chuck Schumer. Democratic strategist Joel Payne and Republican strategist Matt Mowers join "The Takeout" to discuss.

item.title: Nvidia's stock dives as board weighs move to oust Jensen Huang
item.description: Nvidia shares fall sharply in after-hours trading as the company's board considers whether to remove Jensen Huang as CEO.

item.title: Ex-NFL coach Rex Ryan surrenders to Nashville police on hit-and-run charges
item.description: Former NFL head coach Rex Ryan turned himself in to Nashville police on Wednesday on allegations he was involved in a hit-and-run in which authorities said he struck two pedestrians. Tom Hanson reports.

item.title: SS United States to become world's largest artificial reef
item.description: The 1,000-foot long SS United States is being sent to the bottom of the ocean in a controlled, explosive-free sinking that is taking place about 20 nautical miles off the Gulf Coast of Florida.

item.title: 11/11: CBS Evening News
item.description: Several people were killed in a Brooklyn building collapse; Nvidia's board is preparing to oust CEO Jensen Huang, sources say.

item.title: Veterans coming home with CTE | 60 Minutes Archive
item.description: In 2018, 60 Minutes reported on CTE, a degenerative brain disease known for impacting athletes who suffer concussions that is now showing up in soldiers returning from combat.

item.title: 11/11: The Takeout with Major Garrett
item.description: Details on the vote count in Mississippi's Senate race; Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent moved to military base after Iran threats.

item.title: SNAP proposal would increase food insecurity, critics say
item.description: Anti-hunger advocates are blasting a proposed change to SNAP rules that could cut off more than 6 million people from access to federal food aid.

item.title: Nvidia short-seller warned of Jensen Huang's ties to suspected spy
item.description: A small investment firm issued a report about Nvidia in May that foreshadowed issues that have embroiled CEO Jensen Huang in scandal.
